title: Unit 2 test: Differentiation: Definition and Fundamental Properties
author: ab-1
directions: This practice test has two sections. Section I is multiple choice: Part A without a calculator and Part B with a graphing calculator. Section II is free response: Part A with a graphing calculator and Part B without one. Show your work on free-response questions; answers without supporting work may not earn full credit. Unless a question says otherwise, angles are in radians, exact answers are expected without a calculator, and calculator answers are given to three decimal places. Results are raw points for practice only.

A filled point sits near (2, 0.74), where a curve begins that rises, becomes vertical as it passes through (4, 2), and continues to a filled point at (5, 3).
Graph of y = g(x) for −4 ≤ x ≤ 4 made of three segments joining the points (−4, −2), (0, 2), (2, 2), and (4, −2).

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Choose the best answer. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x^3 − 2x on the interval [−1, 2]?

distractorNotes.A: 3 is the change in f without dividing by the interval length.
distractorNotes.C: 4 is f(2), a value rather than a rate.
distractorNotes.D: Reverses the subtraction in the numerator only.

items.prompt: What is lim as h→0 of ((3 + h)^4 − 81)/h?
items.rationale: This is the derivative of x^4 at x = 3: 4·3^3 = 108.

distractorNotes.C: 27 is 3^3, missing the factor 4 from the power rule.

items.prompt:
Selected values of a differentiable function f are shown.

| x | 2 | 4 | 7 | 9 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| f(x) | 10 | 16 | 25 | 28 |

Using the data, what is the best estimate of f′(5)?

distractorNotes.B: 9 is the change in f without dividing by 3.
distractorNotes.C: 18/7 is the average rate over the whole table, not near x = 5.
distractorNotes.D: 5 is the input, not a rate.

items.prompt: The graph of f is shown. At how many values of x in the open interval (−3, 5) is f not differentiable?
items.rationale: f fails to be differentiable at x = −1 (corner), x = 2 (jump discontinuity), and x = 4 (vertical tangent).

distractorNotes.B: Misses the vertical tangent at x = 4, where the slope is unbounded.
distractorNotes.D: Counts a point where f is smooth.

items.prompt: If y = (x^3 − 4√x)/x for x > 0, what is dy/dx?
items.rationale: Divide first: y = x^2 − 4x^(−1/2). Then dy/dx = 2x + 2x^(−3/2).

distractorNotes.A: Sign error: the derivative of −4x^(−1/2) is +2x^(−3/2).
distractorNotes.C: Differentiates the numerator and ignores the denominator.
distractorNotes.D: Multiplies by the exponent incorrectly (−4·(−1) instead of −4·(−1/2)).

items.prompt: Which is an equation of the line tangent to y = e^x + sin x at x = 0?
items.rationale: y(0) = 1 and y′ = e^x + cos x gives y′(0) = 2, so y = 1 + 2x.

distractorNotes.B: Uses slope 1, forgetting the cosine term.
distractorNotes.D: Swaps the slope and the y-intercept.

items.prompt: Suppose f(2) = −3, f′(2) = 4, g(2) = 5, and g′(2) = 2. If h(x) = f(x)g(x), what is h′(2)?

distractorNotes.A: 8 is f′(2)g′(2), which is not the product rule.

items.prompt: If y = (1 + sin x)/cos x, what is the value of dy/dx at x = 0?
items.rationale: Quotient rule: (cos x·cos x − (1 + sin x)(−sin x))/cos^2 x = (1 + sin x)/cos^2 x, which is 1 at x = 0. (Equivalently, y = sec x + tan x.)

distractorNotes.A: Uses only the derivative of sec x, which is 0 at x = 0.
distractorNotes.D: Reverses the order of the quotient-rule numerator.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Choose the best answer. A graphing calculator is required for some questions. If the exact value is not a choice, choose the closest approximation.

items.prompt: Let f(x) = x^3/e^x. What is f′(1)?
The graphs of y = e^x and y = x + 2 intersect at a point with x > 0. What is the slope of the line tangent to y = e^x at that point?
items.rationale: The intersection is at x ≈ 1.146, and the slope of e^x there is e^1.146 ≈ 3.146 (which also equals x + 2).

distractorNotes.A: 1.146 is the x-coordinate, not the slope.
distractorNotes.C: 2 is the y-intercept of the line.
distractorNotes.D: Uses x = 1 instead of the intersection, so x + 2 = 3.

items.prompt: Let f(x) = x^2/(1 + sin x). What is f′(1)?
items.rationale: Quotient rule or numerical derivative: f′(1) = (2(1 + sin 1) − cos 1)/(1 + sin 1)^2 ≈ 0.927.

distractorNotes.C: Divides the derivative of the numerator by the derivative of the denominator.

items.prompt: Let f(x) = x·tan x. For what value of x in (0, 1.5) is f′(x) = 4?
items.rationale: f′(x) = tan x + x sec^2 x. Solving tan x + x sec^2 x = 4 gives x ≈ 0.934.

distractorNotes.A: Solves tan x = 4, dropping the product rule's second term.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: A graphing calculator is required. Show the setup for every calculator result, and give answers to three decimal places with units.

items.prompt:
Rainwater collects in a barrel. The volume of water in the barrel, in liters, t hours after a storm begins is R(t). Selected measurements are shown.

| t (h) | 0 | 1 | 3 | 4 | 6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R(t) (L) | 12.0 | 16.1 | 21.9 | 24.2 | 26.7 |

A model for the volume is M(t) = 12 + 4.5t·e^(−0.1t) liters, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Estimate R′(2) from the table with a difference quotient, and give its units.

rubric.criterion: Uses the data at t = 1 and t = 3: (21.9 − 16.1)/(3 − 1).

steps: The nearest data on either side of t = 2 are at t = 1 and t = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find M′(2), and say what this value tells you about the water in the barrel two hours after the storm begins. Give units.

rubric.criterion: Interprets it: at t = 2 hours the modeled volume is increasing at about 2.947 liters per hour.

parts.answer: M′(2) ≈ 2.947: two hours after the storm begins, the model's volume is increasing at about 2.947 liters per hour.
steps: Use the calculator's numerical derivative of M at t = 2.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the time t in (0, 6) at which the modeled volume is increasing at 2 liters per hour.

rubric.criterion: Uses the calculator to solve, for example by intersecting the graph of M′ with y = 2.

steps: Graph the numerical derivative of M and the line y = 2.
Their intersection in (0, 6) is at t ≈ 3.618.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write an equation of the line tangent to the graph of M at t = 4, and use it to approximate the volume at t = 4.5.

rubric.criterion: Approximates the volume at t = 4.5 as about 24.971 liters (accept 24.970–24.972).

parts.answer: y = 24.066 + 1.810(t − 4); the approximation is about 24.971 liters.

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: No calculator is allowed. Show your work and give exact answers.

items.prompt: The graph of the function g, made of three line segments on −4 ≤ x ≤ 4, is shown.

parts.label: a

rubric.criterion: Applies the product rule: h′(x) = 2x·g(x) + x^2·g′(x).
Reads g(3) = 0 and g′(3) = −2 and gets h′(3) = −18.

steps: On [2, 4], g has slope −2 and g(3) = 0.

rubric.criterion: Applies the quotient rule: k′(x) = (g′(x)e^x − g(x)e^x)/e^(2x).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Decide whether g is differentiable at x = 0. Support your decision with the one-sided limits of the difference quotient (g(x) − g(0))/x as x→0.

rubric.criterion: Finds the left-hand limit of the difference quotient, 1 (the slope of the segment from (−4, −2) to (0, 2)).
Finds the right-hand limit of the difference quotient, 0 (the horizontal segment from (0, 2) to (2, 2)).
Concludes that g is not differentiable at 0 because the one-sided limits differ.

parts.answer: No. As x→0⁻ the difference quotient is 1 (slope of the left segment) and as x→0⁺ it is 0 (the horizontal segment). The one-sided limits differ, so g′(0) does not exist: the graph has a corner at (0, 2), even though g is continuous there.
steps: The one-sided limits 1 and 0 differ, so g is not differentiable at 0; g is continuous there because both sides approach g(0) = 2.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Let m(x) = g(x)·tan x. Find m′(π/3).

rubric.criterion: Applies the product rule, m′(x) = g′(x)tan x + g(x)sec^2 x, with g(π/3) = 2 and g′(π/3) = 0 read from the horizontal segment (0 < π/3 < 2).

steps: π/3 lies between 0 and 2, where g(x) = 2 and g′(x) = 0.
